title: Color primitives
summary: Decisions for a color ramp. The schemes are described. Nothing here calculates a color.

questions.prompt: Which color space do you describe the ramp in?
questions.summary: The space is where you plan steps. Delivery can still be sRGB hex.

options.label: OKLCH
options.why: OKLCH separates lightness from chroma and hue, so you can plan steps by lightness alone.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your tools can read oklch() values.
trade_offs: Older tools may not read oklch()
Some colors fall outside the screen's range and need a fallback

options.label: HSL
options.why: HSL is widely known, and its three parts have familiar names: hue, saturation and lightness.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your team already works in HSL.
trade_offs: Equal HSL steps do not look equal in lightness

options.label: Lab
options.why: CIELAB is a color space from color science, with a lightness axis and two color axes.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you already measure color in Lab.
trade_offs: Hue is less direct than in OKLCH

options.label: sRGB
options.why: sRGB is the standard screen color space behind hex values. It is the usual delivery space.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you only need hex values and simple mixes.
trade_offs: Ramps can look uneven

questions.why_care: It decides how your color steps are described, and it unlocks even steps and hue shifts in OKLCH.

questions.prompt: How do you space the steps?
questions.summary: The distance metric is a rule for the ramp, not a result.

options.label: Equal deltaE2000
options.why: Steps are spaced so the perceived difference between neighbors is equal, measured with CIEDE2000.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you measure steps with CIEDE2000.
trade_offs: The math is harder to explain
Needs OKLCH or Lab as the color space
options.formula: OKLCH or Lab steps, equal deltaE2000.

options.label: Equal lightness
options.summary: The same lightness change each step.
options.why: Each step changes lightness by the same amount in the chosen color space.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you want a plain, even ramp.
trade_offs: Perceived gaps can still vary
options.formula: Equal lightness steps in the chosen color space.

options.label: Contrast steps
options.summary: Steps spaced by contrast against the light end.
options.why: Each step targets a contrast gap against the lightest color.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if contrast between steps matters more than even hue spacing.
trade_offs: The ramp can look less even
options.formula: Steps spaced by contrast against the light end.

questions.prompt: Which way do the color step numbers run?
questions.summary: This question references the global scheme. One option is overridden here.

overrides.label: 50 to 1000
overrides.summary: Color steps use 50 to 1000. A low number is a light color.
overrides.why: Color steps in this pack use the 50 to 1000 names, and a low number stays a light color.
overrides.when_to_choose: Choose this if the color steps should match Tailwind-style names.
trade_offs: You give up a 100 to 0 lightness name
overrides.formula: Color stops from 50 through 1000. Lightness falls as the number rises.

questions.why_care: It decides whether a low number means light or dark, so the names match what your team already says.

questions.prompt: How many steps are in the ramp?
questions.summary: The count is a name. The recipe can also store a custom number.

options.label: 9 steps
options.why: Nine steps give you a plain 100 to 900 scale.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you do not need a 50 or a 950 step.
trade_offs: You lose the very light and very dark ends

options.label: 10 steps
options.why: Ten steps add a lighter 50 in front of 100 through 900, as in Tailwind v2.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you want a 50 and no 950.
trade_offs: The two ends are not symmetric

options.label: 11 steps
options.why: Eleven steps run from 50 through 950, as in the Tailwind color scale.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if people expect both a 50 and a 950.
trade_offs: You have more tokens to name

options.label: 12 steps
options.why: Twelve steps match scales built on twelve slots, such as 1 to 12.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your references use twelve colors.
trade_offs: Names differ from a 50 to 950 scale

options.label: Custom count
options.why: You set the number of steps, from 5 to 16, and the recipe stores the count.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if 9, 10, 11 or 12 steps do not fit.
trade_offs: A custom count is harder to share
options.formula: A stored step count between 5 and 16.

questions.why_care: The count sets how finely you can name light-to-dark colors, and how many tokens you keep tidy.

questions.prompt: How does lightness change along the ramp?
questions.summary: The curve is a description of the lightness path.

options.label: Linear
options.why: Lightness changes by an even amount from the light end to the dark end.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you want the plainest path.
trade_offs: The middle can look uneven
options.formula: Linear lightness from the light end to the dark end.

options.label: Ease
options.why: An ease curve changes lightness more slowly near the light and dark ends.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the ends should move more slowly.
trade_offs: Steps in the middle sit farther apart

options.label: Perceptual
options.why: A perceptual curve puts more steps in the middle of the ramp, where most UI surfaces sit.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if most of your UI sits in the middle of the ramp.
trade_offs: The ends move faster
options.formula: Perceptual lightness curve with more middle steps.

questions.prompt: How do chroma and hue move as the ramp darkens?
questions.summary: A shift is a described rule, not a generated color.

options.label: No shift
options.summary: Chroma and hue stay at the seed.
options.why: Chroma and hue stay at the seed. Only lightness changes.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the seed color should not drift.
trade_offs: Dark steps can look dull or neon

options.label: Chroma taper
options.why: Chroma is lower at the light and dark ends and fuller in the middle.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the ends should look softer.
trade_offs: The middle can look more saturated than the brand

options.label: Warm hue shift
options.why: Darker steps shift a little toward warm hues.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the brand should stay warm as it darkens.
trade_offs: A cool brand can look muddy
Needs OKLCH as the color space
options.formula: Hue shifts warmer as lightness falls.

options.label: Cool hue shift
options.why: Darker steps shift a little toward cool hues.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if the brand should cool as it darkens.
trade_offs: A warm brand can look grey
Needs OKLCH as the color space
options.formula: Hue shifts cooler as lightness falls.

questions.prompt: How do you record the seed color?
questions.summary: The seed is stored on the recipe. Open DS does not turn it into a ramp.

options.label: Hex seed
options.why: A hex seed is one six-digit value. The recipe records it and does not calculate a ramp.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you have one brand hex.
trade_offs: Hex hides lightness and chroma

options.label: OKLCH parts
options.summary: Lightness, chroma, and hue as numbers.
options.why: You record lightness, chroma and hue as numbers. The recipe does not convert them.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your seed is already in OKLCH.
trade_offs: Many people cannot read the numbers
Needs OKLCH as the color space
options.formula: Stored OKLCH components. No conversion is run.

questions.prompt: How do you name a surface and the color on it?
questions.summary: One pairing rule: a surface and its on-surface color.

options.label: surface and on-surface
options.summary: Each surface has one paired on-color.
options.why: One rule names a surface and the color on it: surface and on-surface.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if text and its background must stay paired.
trade_offs: You use one naming scheme only
options.formula: Pair {name} with on-{name}. The required pair is surface and on-surface.

requires.question: theme-shape
requires.reason: Surface and on-surface stay paired in light and dark, so those are modifiers on one theme.

options.label: Unrelated names
options.summary: Background and text names do not show the pair.
options.why: Background and text use names that do not show the pair, such as `bg-white` and `text-gray-950` in Tailwind.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if your files already use unrelated color names.
trade_offs: You give up names that show the pair, as in Material's primary and on primary

questions.why_care: Naming pairs together makes it obvious which text color belongs on which background.
